minutes.headline: Open Space Committee heard how tax title and foreclosure work and picked town parcels to research; no land decisions.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the tax collector explain the tax lien, foreclosure and auction process and what "tax title" and "owners unknown" mean in the assessor's database. It then reviewed more town-owned parcels and chose a short list to research (Lake Shirley area parcels, the primary school and Woodruff/Pleasant Street history, and West Street). It also discussed the town manager's request that the Select Board be told before other boards are contacted.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee made no land decisions; it spent most of the meeting on how town-owned land is reviewed and researched.
The tax collector explained the tax lien, foreclosure and auction process, and what "tax title" and "owners unknown" mean in the assessor's database.
Members agreed to research the Lake Shirley group of town parcels and to contact the office of fishing and boating access.
Further research was assigned on the primary school (MEPA process), the Woodruff property records, and a West Street parcel.
The committee discussed the town manager's request that the Select Board be told before other boards are contacted; no resolution was reached.

why_it_matters: Tax-title and foreclosed parcels are one way land can come into town ownership, and a committee list of parcels to research is an early step before any proposal that could reach a Town Meeting vote on land use or purchase.
The notification request shows a process question: how a committee reaches other boards about town land, which shapes how quickly any parcel proposal could advance.
